## Summary
Fixed the "no streams" bug (GUI/`pythonw` case where `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` is `None`): `click.echo` (and the `_termui_impl` consumers of the default streams) no longer raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'/'flush'`; they become no-ops / write to a throwaway `StringIO`. Only `src/click/_compat.py`, `src/click/_termui_impl.py`, `src/click/utils.py` were touched (core.py untouched, tests/ untouched).

## (a) Buggy code (exact file+line, pre-fix)
- `src/click/utils.py:249-253` (`echo`): resolves `file = _default_text_stdout()/_default_text_stderr()` but never checks for `None`; then `file.write(out)` (line 298) / `file.flush()` (line 269) blow up.
- `src/click/_compat.py:587-607` (`_make_cached_stream_func`): `src_func()` may return `None` (e.g. `sys.stdout is None`); no `None` guard, and annotations claim a non-optional `t.TextIO`.
- `src/click/_termui_impl.py:63-65` (`ProgressBar.__init__`) and `:346-348` (`pager`): assign the result of `_default_text_stdout()` unconditionally, then use it (`echo(self.label, file=self.file)`, `_nullpager(stdout, ...)` → `stream.write`).

## (b) Root cause
`_default_text_stdout()`/`_default_text_stderr()` legitimately return `None` when `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` is `None`: `_force_correct_text_writer(None, ...)` → `_is_binary_writer(None)` is False, `_is_compatible_text_stream(None, ...)` is True but `_stream_is_misconfigured(None)` is True, `_find_binary_writer(None)` returns `None`, so the original `None` is returned. Every caller assumed a real text stream and dereferenced it.
